Expected the long tail to have messier version metadata; a full-ecosystem census proved the prediction wrong
97% of both head and tail are clean PEP 440; the only gap is cadence, not version strings
Baseline head-vs-tail census of wheel presence across 6,000 latest releases
The long tail ships wheels, but 95% of its wheel-shippers ship a single pure-Python wheel
The long tail is 7x more likely to link to no source code at all
Runtime dependency footprint is identical head vs tail; the entire gap is optional extras
Popular packages carry more metadata but nearly 9x more legacy reStructuredText READMEs than the long tail
The long tail caps the Python version MORE than the head
Popularity does not buy frequent releases; it buys regular ones
Popular packages write terser one-liner summaries but much longer READMEs
72% of popular declarers say Production/Stable vs 23% of the tail
The head clings to legacy rST READMEs 29% vs 5%, not more modern Markdown
PyPI's JSON API synthesizes a project_urls Homepage from the legacy Home-page field, so it cannot measure PEP 753 migration
Popular packages declare themselves typed 1.8x more, but the Typing :: Typed label undercounts real typing
The long tail flags non-English languages more (7.7% vs 2.4% of declarers), not the head
The long tail relies on 'OS Independent' more (81% vs 72%); the head names real platforms
Popular packages are not for a broader audience: 97% of head declarers tag Developers vs 85%
Popular packages choose barely deeper Topic paths (3.29 vs 3.25) and the extra depth is template boilerplate

The long tail is more parse-ambiguous (41% vs 38%) despite the head using commas and phrases more

A published 29% exact-pin share drops to 9-17% on fresh latest-release data
